title: Buddy Tate, Jay McShann and Michael's Pub
summary: Freeman recalls Buddy Tate coming onstage at a Belgian festival, Tate's European popularity, and meeting Jay McShann at Newport.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Wonderful. Do you see anything of Yannick Bruynoghe, you know, Yannick who is the film man and he also wrote that book on Big Bill Broonzy! Do you know who I mean.

I know who you mean. I think I did meet him once in -- I played a -- I did a festival one of the summer festivals in Belgium and a very interesting thing happened. I looked out of the wings and there is Buddy Tate and I said, 'How about getting your horn up,' which he did and came up and played a half hour with me, and it was marvelous. He's a great guy and Buddy comes over quite a lot.
Yes, I know he does, and he's worked a lot with Benny too.
He's made a big name for himself in Europe, it's great to see.
Couldn't have a nicer person, and he

right now he's -- he worked with Jay McShann at Michael's Pub recently and they made a session for Atlantic and they also made a session for -- well, while they were live in Toronto, marvelcus, really very wonderful.
I met Jay McShann and for the first time at the Newport Jazz Festival last July. And Buddy was there, too.
Did you, for the first time, isn't that funny. He's a marvelous piano player.
Yes, and Michael's Pub is doing very well, is it?
Yes, it's doing well. It's proving to be quite a showcase for the right kind of music and so on.
